native_mcp_support.notes: Supported via 'Connectors' (beta): MCP-compatible servers registered via API or Studio and exposed as tools to the model in conversations and Agents. Transport is managed server-side; client does not need local MCP transport.

skills_concept.value: Agents — pre-configured model instances with system prompt, tools, and completion params; persistent Conversations API tracks turn history server-side
skills_concept.notes: Agents are created via POST /v1/agents and referenced by agent_id in Conversations. System prompts and tool stubs are injected at conversation start and count as input tokens. Mistral Vibe CLI also exposes 'agents-skills' concept for CLI-based agents.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Not published in model card or docs as of 2026-06-21.

context_window_tokens.notes: Confirmed in Known Limitations context-window table and model card.

input_output_shared.notes: Known Limitations states: 'Token counts include both input and output tokens.'

max_input_tokens.notes: Not published as a separate cap. Effective max input = context_window - max_tokens_requested. No documented separate input limit.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Mistral docs state default varies by model; query /models endpoint. Not published as a fixed number in model card.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Bounded by context_window_tokens minus input. No separate published hard cap other than the 256k window. Retrieve via /models endpoint.

extended_context.notes: No extended/beta context beyond 256k documented for this model.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Mistral Medium 3.5 is not documented as a reasoning/thinking model; no reasoning token billing documented.

tokenizer_family.notes: Mistral's tokenization docs describe V3-Tekken as the current tokenizer for modern models, built on tiktoken rather than SentencePiece. mistral-common README states 'we only release Tekken tokenizers for recent models'.

tokenizer_public.notes: mistral-common is open-source (Apache-2.0) and includes tokenizer code and weights downloadable from PyPI or Hugging Face Hub.

tokenizer_access.value: pip install mistral-common; tokenizer downloadable from HF Hub via mistral-common[hf-hub]

count_tokens_method.value: from mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer; tok = MistralTokenizer.v3(); tokens = tok.encode(text)
count_tokens_method.notes: mistral-common provides encode/decode plus tool-call-aware tokenization. For exact per-request counts including tool defs, use the library locally with the Tekken tokenizer file.

image_token_rule.notes: Model supports vision (image input) per model card. Precise token-per-image tiling rule not published in docs as of 2026-06-21.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio transcription listed as a feature on the model card, but tokens-per-second rule not documented.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Rough industry estimate for BPE tokenizers on English text. Use mistral-common for accurate counts.

function_calling.notes: Function Calling listed as a supported feature in model card.

native_mcp.notes: Via 'Connectors' beta: register any MCP-compatible server URL; tools are discovered and called by the model. Currently beta; interface may change.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: parallel_tool_calls parameter documented (default: true). Model may emit multiple tool calls per turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: Known Limitations: 'Maximum number of tools per request: 128.'

max_tools_practical.notes: No Mistral-specific empirical study found. Using community consensus of ~30-50 tools before accuracy degradation (Berkeley FCL, general practitioner reports). Treat as indicative only.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tool spec uses {type: 'function', function: {name, description, parameters}} — identical to OpenAI function-calling JSON schema.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Known Limitations: 'Tool descriptions are included in the token count. Long descriptions reduce available context for messages.'

tool_search_deferral.notes: No documented lazy/deferred tool loading in Mistral API. Connectors can be registered selectively per conversation, which provides coarse control, but no automatic deferral mechanism.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character cap on function/tool names documented in Mistral API spec or Known Limitations as of 2026-06-21. Note: Connector (MCP server) names have a 64-char cap (alphanumeric+underscore+dash), but this is the registry name, not the tool function name itself.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on tool description length. Known Limitations states descriptions count toward the token budget, but imposes no hard character limit.

max_request_size.notes: No byte/MB payload cap documented for POST /v1/chat/completions. File upload endpoint has a 512 MB cap, but that is a separate endpoint. Chat request size is effectively bounded by the 256k token context window.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented cap on individual tool result size. Tool results (role: 'tool' messages) count against the shared 256k context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: parallel_tool_calls is a boolean parameter (default: true); no numeric cap on simultaneous tool calls published. Known Limitations: 'Parallel function calls are supported but may return calls in any order.'

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No documented cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn or per agentic loop. Function calling docs show an example loop ('recursively call the model until it generates a final answer') with no stated limit.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented cap on the number of Connectors (MCP servers) that can be registered in a workspace or attached to a single conversation/agent. Connector list uses cursor-based pagination, suggesting potentially large counts are expected.

max_total_tools.notes: No aggregate-across-connectors tool count documented separately. The API-level hard cap is 128 tools per request (max_tools_hard). If multiple connectors expose tools, all count toward that 128 limit.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Connector (MCP server registry) names: max 64 chars, alphanumeric with underscores and dashes only (source: https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/connectors/management). Tool function name cap: not published. No documented limit on tool JSON schema depth, property count, or total tool definition byte size. Tool descriptions count toward the 256k token budget (Known Limitations).
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Rate limits enforced per API key (not per workspace): requests-per-second and tokens-per-minute independently. Returns 429 on breach. Check X-RateLimit-Remaining header. Batch API does not count against real-time limits. Connectors are beta (interface may change). Prompt caching: the API exposes a prompt_cache_key param (cached tokens billed at 10% of input price) as of 2026-06-21, though this was not prominently documented at the time of the initial skills_context.prompt_caching capture — verify current pricing page. Connector tool schemas are loaded into context when a Connector is referenced; large MCP servers with many tools will consume substantial context budget.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: Agents API allows creating pre-configured model instances with system prompts and tools. These are the Mistral skills analog.

skills_loading_model.notes: Agent instructions (system prompt) and tool list are fixed at agent creation time and injected at conversation start. No progressive disclosure mechanism documented.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Agent system prompts and tool definitions are injected as input tokens at the start of each conversation. Connector tool schemas are also loaded into context when a Connector is referenced in a conversation.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System prompt token cost depends on the agent's 'instructions' field content. Not a fixed overhead — developer-controlled. Tool descriptions additionally reduce available context per Known Limitations.

prompt_caching.notes: No prompt caching / prefix caching feature documented in Mistral API as of 2026-06-21. Not mentioned in pricing, model cards, or API reference.

memory_feature.notes: Conversations API stores turn history server-side by default (opt-out with store=False). This persistent history is replayed as input tokens on each continuation, growing context over a session.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: No prompt caching feature; no cached input price tier documented.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API provides 50% discount for asynchronous inference. Batch does not count against real-time rate limits.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billing rule (tiles/tokens per image) not published. Audio transcription billed separately (audio endpoint). Check pricing page for any per-image or per-minute surcharges.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Not a documented reasoning model; no reasoning token billing.

models.notes: Mistral Medium 3.5 (v26.04) is the latest and most capable general-purpose model as of 2026-06-21. It is also released as open weights under a Modified MIT license (HF: mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5), but this file covers the hosted API only. API string: 'mistral-medium-3-5' or 'mistral-medium-latest' (verify via /models).
